body: Income Tax Act 2007 section MA 4: If a calculation under Part M produces a result that is negative for the amount of a tax credit or the amount of a component of a credit, the amount of the credit or component is zero.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 1: A person who qualifies under section MC 2 is entitled to the abating WFF tax credit equal to the formula family tax credit + (in-work tax credit or child tax credit) + parental tax credit - credit abatement. Family tax credit is calculated under section MD 3. In-work tax credit is calculated under section MD 10 if the person is entitled to it; otherwise child tax credit may apply. Credit abatement includes family credit abatement calculated under section MD 13 and relevant parental tax credit abatement.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 2: The Commissioner applies family credit abatement first to reduce the family tax credit, second to reduce the in-work tax credit or child tax credit, and third to reduce the parental tax credit.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 3: Family tax credit is calculated by the formula prescribed amount x days / 365. Prescribed amount is the sum of $7,921 for the eldest dependent child for whom the person is a principal caregiver during the entitlement period, and $6,454 for each other dependent child for whom the person is a principal caregiver. Days is the number of days in the entitlement period. A family tax credit must be reduced in proportion to the time in the entitlement period that a dependent child spends in the exclusive care of another person who qualifies under section MC 2.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 10: In-work tax credit is calculated by the formula (amount A + amount B x (children - 3)) x weekly periods / 52. Amount A is $7,670. Amount B is $780. Children is the greater of 3 and the number of children for whom the person is allowed the in-work tax credit. Weekly periods is the number of whole periods of 1 week in the relevant entitlement period or continuous period for which the earner requirement is met.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MD 13: Family credit abatement is calculated by the formula full-year abatement x days / 365. Full-year abatement is 27.5 cents for each complete dollar of family scheme income over $44,900 for the relationship period containing the entitlement period, applying either to the person or to the person and spouse, civil union partner, or de facto partner. Days is the number of days in the entitlement period excluding days of protected family tax credit months.

Income Tax Act 2007 section ME 1: Minimum family tax credit is calculated by the formula (prescribed amount - net family scheme income) x weekly periods / 52. Prescribed amount is $36,604. Net family scheme income is calculated using section ME 3 for the relationship period. Weekly periods is the number of periods of 1 week in the entitlement period for which the person is a full-time earner.

Income Tax Act 2007 section ME 3: Net family scheme income is calculated by the formula adjusted income - adjusted liability + amount received - amount paid. Adjusted income includes the person's family scheme income for the tax year attributable to the number of weeks in which the person is a full-time earner, annualised by multiplying by 52 divided by the number of weeks in the relationship period for which the person is a full-time earner. Adjusted liability is the income tax liability treating adjusted income as the person's net income.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MG 1: Best Start tax credit entitlement applies for an entitlement period for a dependent child if the person qualifies under section MC 2, is a principal caregiver, the dependent child is aged less than 3 years old, and the birth or expected due date test is met. The formula is Best Start tax credit - credit abatement, using section MG 2 for the credit and section MG 3 for abatement.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MG 2: Best Start tax credit for the entitlement period for the dependent child is calculated by the formula prescribed amount x days / 365. Prescribed amount is $4,041 for the dependent child. Days is the number of days in the entitlement period. A Best Start tax credit must be reduced in proportion to the time in the entitlement period that the dependent child spends in the exclusive care of another qualifying person.

Income Tax Act 2007 section MG 3: Best Start credit abatement is calculated by the formula full-year abatement x days / 365. Full-year abatement is 21 cents for each complete dollar of family scheme income over $79,000 for the relationship period containing the entitlement period, applying either to the person or to the person and spouse, civil union partner, or de facto partner. Days excludes days on which the dependent child is less than 1 year old if born before 1 April 2026, and days of protected Best Start tax credit months.

Taxation (Annual Rates for 2025-26, Compliance Simplification, and Remedial Measures) Act 2026 section 2: section 105(1) comes into force on 1 April 2026. Section 105(2) comes into force on a single date set by Order in Council. If section 105(2) has not come into force by 1 April 2027, it comes into force then.

Taxation (Annual Rates for 2025-26, Compliance Simplification, and Remedial Measures) Act 2026 section 105: In section MD 10(3)(a), replace 5,070 with 7,670. In section MD 10(3)(a), replace 7,670 with 5,070.
